items.followUp: Define addition of forces and explain how the head-to-tail rule determines the resultant of two perpendicular forces. Include a labelled figure.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of addition of forces.
rubric.description: Defines addition of forces as vector addition used to find a single resultant force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining addition as vector addition that gives the resultant.

rubric.why: Checks the head-to-tail construction for the perpendicular components.
rubric.description: Places the tail of Fy at the head of Fx, with Fy perpendicular to Fx.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the placement and perpendicular relationship of the components.

rubric.why: Checks that the resultant is shown as the diagonal joining the start and end of the component vectors.
rubric.description: Shows the resultant R as the diagonal from the tail of Fx to the head of Fy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying or drawing the diagonal resultant.

rubric.why: Checks the magnitude or direction relation for the resultant of perpendicular components.
rubric.description: Gives the resultant magnitude or its direction relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct magnitude formula or direction formula.

modelAnswer: Addition of forces is the vector addition of two or more forces to find their single resultant force.
Using the head-to-tail rule, draw Fy from the head of Fx, perpendicular to Fx (at 90°).
The resultant R is the diagonal drawn from the tail of Fx to the head of Fy.
Its magnitude is R = √(Fx² + Fy²), and its direction is given by tan θ = Fy/Fx.

items.followUp: A screw gauge has a pitch of 0.5 mm and 50 divisions on its circular scale. Find its least count.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of pitch, which is needed to determine the least count.
rubric.description: Defines pitch as the distance moved by the screw in one complete rotation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating what pitch represents.

rubric.why: Checks the relation used to calculate the least count.
rubric.description: Gives least count = pitch divided by the number of divisions on the circular scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: Pitch is the distance moved by the screw in one complete rotation.
Least count = pitch / number of divisions on the circular scale.
